queries: WITH r AS (SELECT m.MediaTypeId, m.Name, 1.0 * SUM(t.Bytes) / SUM(t.Milliseconds) AS rate, COUNT(*) AS track_count FROM Track t JOIN MediaType m ON m.MediaTypeId = t.MediaTypeId GROUP BY m.MediaTypeId, m.Name), a AS (SELECT AVG(rate) AS avg_rate FROM r) SELECT r.Name, r.rate, r.track_count, r.rate - a.avg_rate AS above_average FROM r CROSS JOIN a WHERE r.rate > a.avg_rate

assumptions.assumption: A media type's rate is total Bytes divided by total Milliseconds across its tracks (ratio of sums), not an average of per-track ratios.
Tracks with a matching media type means an inner join of Track to MediaType, so media types with no tracks are excluded and each remaining type counts once in the average.
Track count includes every track of the type, even those with NULL Bytes (SUM ignores NULL Bytes, but their Milliseconds still count in the rate's denominator).
The average is the simple unweighted mean of the per-type rates, and no rounding is applied.

alternatives.interpretation: A media type's rate is the average of each track's own Bytes/Milliseconds ratio (tracks with NULL Bytes are ignored in the rate), instead of the ratio of totals.
alternatives.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT m.MediaTypeId, m.Name, AVG(1.0 * t.Bytes / t.Milliseconds) AS rate, COUNT(*) AS track_count FROM Track t JOIN MediaType m ON m.MediaTypeId = t.MediaTypeId GROUP BY m.MediaTypeId, m.Name), a AS (SELECT AVG(rate) AS avg_rate FROM r) SELECT r.Name, r.rate, r.track_count, r.rate - a.avg_rate AS above_average FROM r CROSS JOIN a WHERE r.rate > a.avg_rate

assumptions.assumption: A media type's rate is total Bytes divided by total Milliseconds across its tracks (a pooled ratio), not the mean of per-track ratios.
Only media types with at least one track are included, because 'tracks that have a matching media type' is an inner join. The average is taken over those types, each counted once.
Tracks with NULL Bytes still count in track_count, but their Milliseconds are left out of the rate denominator so the numerator and denominator cover the same tracks.
'How far above' means the plain difference rate minus average rate, not a percentage. Nothing is rounded.

alternatives.interpretation: Each media type's rate is the average of per-track Bytes/Milliseconds ratios instead of the pooled ratio.
alternatives.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT m.MediaTypeId, m.Name, AVG(CAST(t.Bytes AS REAL) / t.Milliseconds) AS rate, COUNT(*) AS track_count FROM MediaType m JOIN Track t ON t.MediaTypeId = m.MediaTypeId GROUP BY m.MediaTypeId, m.Name), a AS (SELECT AVG(rate) AS avg_rate FROM r) SELECT r.Name, r.rate, r.track_count, r.rate - a.avg_rate AS above_average FROM r CROSS JOIN a WHERE r.rate > a.avg_rate ORDER BY above_average DESC

assumptions.assumption: A media type's rate is total Bytes divided by total Milliseconds across its tracks (ratio of sums), computed in floating point and not rounded.
'Matching media type' means an inner join of Track to MediaType, so media types with no tracks are excluded from the average and the output.

The average is the simple mean of the per-media-type rates, with each type counted once. Track_count counts all of a type's tracks, including any with NULL Bytes, which would be skipped by the Bytes sum.

alternatives.interpretation: A media type's rate is the mean of the per-track Bytes/Milliseconds ratios, instead of total bytes over total milliseconds.
alternatives.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT m.MediaTypeId, m.Name, AVG(1.0*t.Bytes/t.Milliseconds) AS rate, COUNT(*) AS track_count FROM Track t JOIN MediaType m ON m.MediaTypeId = t.MediaTypeId GROUP BY m.MediaTypeId, m.Name) SELECT Name, rate, track_count, rate - (SELECT AVG(rate) FROM r) AS above_average FROM r WHERE rate > (SELECT AVG(rate) FROM r)
